# ADR 0010: Reference table ids become identity columns

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** `instruments/questions/choices/scoring_rules/risk_rules/flow_transitions`
used explicit, migration-assigned ids (`ValueGeneratedNever()`) since they were
originally seed-only reference data. Phase 4 needs the admin API to insert new
rows into these same tables at runtime, and nothing should have to compute the
next id itself.

**Decision:** All six id columns became Postgres `GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS
IDENTITY` (migration `MakeReferenceIdsIdentity`). "By default" (not "always")
so the existing seed rows' explicit ids stay valid. The same migration bumps
every sequence to start at 1000 via `setval(pg_get_serial_sequence(...), 1000,
false)`, since converting a column to identity does not itself move the
sequence past whatever explicit values already exist (seed data tops out at
244, for choices).

**Consequence:** Verified against real Postgres: a plain insert with no id
returns 1000, confirmed with zero collisions against seed data. Any future
seed data added via migration must keep its explicit ids below 1000, or the
headroom assumption breaks.
